topics.title: Overview, Objectives & Key Definitions
topics.concept:
Unit Overview

Unit 1 ended with the idea that the instantaneous rate of change is a limit of secant slopes. This unit turns that idea into a precise, computable object: the derivative. You will define the derivative as a limit, then build a toolkit of rules — power, product, quotient, and the derivatives of the basic trig functions — that lets you differentiate quickly without returning to the limit each time.

Differentiation is the single most-used skill in AP Calculus. Almost every later unit assumes you can differentiate fluently and correctly. This unit is about 10–12% of the exam on its own, but its reach is total.

Big picture: The derivative f'(x) measures how fast f changes, and geometrically it is the slope of the tangent line.

Learning Objectives

You will be able to:

  • Define f'(x) using the limit of a difference quotient (both forms).
  • Interpret the derivative as a slope of a tangent line and an instantaneous rate of change.
  • Estimate derivatives from graphs and tables.
  • Explain the relationship between differentiability and continuity (and where differentiability fails).
  • Apply the Power Rule, constant multiple, and sum/difference rules.
  • Differentiate sin, cos, tan, cot, sec, csc.
  • Apply the Product Rule and Quotient Rule.
  • Compute higher-order derivatives.
  • Perform implicit differentiation and differentiate inverse functions.

Prerequisite Concepts

  • Limits and the difference quotient (Unit 1).
  • Exponent rules, including negative and fractional exponents.
  • Trig values and identities.
  • Function composition and the meaning of an inverse function.

Key Definitions

  • Difference quotient: (f(x + h) − f(x)) / h — the average rate of change over a step of size h.
  • Derivative (limit definition): f'(x) = lim_{h→0} (f(x + h) − f(x)) / h
  • Alternate (point) form: f'(a) = lim_{x→a} (f(x) − f(a)) / (x − a)
  • Notations: f'(x), dy/dx, y', d/dx[f(x)], and for higher orders f''(x), d²y/dx².
  • Differentiable at a: the limit defining f'(a) exists (the graph has a single, non-vertical tangent line there).
  • Higher-order derivative: the derivative of a derivative; f'' is the second derivative, f''' the third, etc.

quiz.q: The position of a particle moving along a coordinate axis is given by s(t) = t^3 - 3t^2 + 2t. What is the average rate of change of position on the interval [0, 2]?
quiz.explanation: The average rate of change is [s(2) - s(0)] / (2 - 0). s(2) = 8 - 12 + 4 = 0. s(0) = 0. Thus, (0 - 0) / 2 = 0.

quiz.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the definition of the derivative of f(x) at x = a?
quiz.explanation: Both lim_{h→0} [f(a+h) - f(a)] / h and lim_{x→a} [f(x) - f(a)] / (x - a) are standard limit definitions for f'(a).

quiz.q: If f(2) = 5 and f'(2) = -3, what is the best linear approximation for f(2.1)?
quiz.explanation: The tangent line approximation is L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a). L(2.1) = 5 + (-3)(2.1 - 2) = 5 - 0.3 = 4.7.

quiz.q: Let f(x) = |x - 2|. Which of the following is true at x = 2?
options: f is continuous and differentiable at x = 2.
f is continuous but not differentiable at x = 2.
f is differentiable but not continuous at x = 2.
f is neither continuous nor differentiable at x = 2.
quiz.explanation: The graph of f(x) = |x - 2| has a sharp corner (v-shape) at x = 2. It is continuous everywhere, but the derivative does not exist at the corner.

quiz.q: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^(1/2) - 3x^(-2).

topics.title: Important Theorems & Formulas
topics.concept:
Important Theorems

Differentiability implies continuity. If f is differentiable at a, then f is continuous at a. The converse is false: a function can be continuous but not differentiable (e.g., |x| at x = 0).

Where differentiability fails: at corners (like |x|), cusps (like x^(2/3) at 0), vertical tangents, and any discontinuity.

Inverse Function Derivative Theorem. If f is differentiable and one-to-one with inverse g, then g'(a) = 1 / f'(g(a)), provided f'(g(a)) ≠ 0.

Important Formulas

Basic rules (c constant, n any real number):

  • Constant: d/dx[c] = 0
  • Power Rule: d/dx[x^n] = n·x^(n−1)
  • Constant multiple: d/dx[c·f] = c·f'
  • Sum/Difference: d/dx[f ± g] = f' ± g'

Product Rule: d/dx[f·g] = f'·g + f·g'

Quotient Rule: d/dx[f/g] = (f'·g − f·g') / g² (remember: "low d-high minus high d-low, over low squared")

Trig derivatives:

  • d/dx[sin x] = cos x
  • d/dx[cos x] = −sin x
  • d/dx[tan x] = sec² x
  • d/dx[cot x] = −csc² x
  • d/dx[sec x] = sec x · tan x
  • d/dx[csc x] = −csc x · cot x

quiz.q: Find the derivative of f(x) = (x^2 + 1) / (x - 1).
If f(x) = x^3 + x - 2, and g is the inverse function of f, what is g'(0)?
The derivative of f(x) = √(x + 3) at x = 1 using the definition of the derivative is:
A function is continuous at a point but not differentiable. Which of the following could be true?
options: The function has a vertical tangent at that point.
The function has a removable discontinuity at that point.
The function has a jump discontinuity at that point.
The function is not defined at that point.
quiz.explanation: A vertical tangent (e.g., f(x) = ∛x at x = 0) makes a function continuous but non-differentiable. The other options describe discontinuities or undefined points.

quiz.q: The derivative of f(x) = (x² + 1)(x³ - 2) is:

topics.title: Concept Explanations & Solved Examples
topics.concept:
Concept Explanations

Two forms of the derivative (2.2). The h → 0 form gives the derivative function f'(x); the x → a form gives the derivative value f'(a) directly. Recognizing a limit as one of these forms is a common AP multiple-choice task: e.g., lim_{h→0} ((2+h)⁴ − 16)/h is exactly f'(2) for f(x) = x⁴, which is 32.

Differentiability vs. continuity (2.4). Differentiability is stronger than continuity. To be differentiable, a function must be continuous and smooth (no corner, cusp, or vertical tangent). For a piecewise function, check both that the pieces meet (continuity) and that their one-sided derivatives match (smoothness).

Choosing a rule (2.11). Read the structure of the expression:

  • A single power → Power Rule.
  • A product of two functions of x → Product Rule.
  • A quotient → Quotient Rule.
  • (A function inside another → Chain Rule, formally Unit 3, but often needed alongside these.)

Implicit differentiation (2.13). When y is defined implicitly (e.g., x² + y² = 25), differentiate both sides with respect to x, treating y as a function of x (so d/dx[y²] = 2y·(dy/dx)), then solve for dy/dx.

Inverse-function derivatives (2.14). You do not need a formula for the inverse itself. Use g'(a) = 1 / f'(g(a)): find the input where f outputs a, then reciprocate the derivative of f there.

Worked Examples

Example 1 (Limit definition). Find f'(x) for f(x) = x² from the definition. lim_{h→0} ((x+h)² − x²)/h = lim_{h→0} (2xh + h²)/h = lim_{h→0} (2x + h) = 2x.

Example 2 (Power Rule with fractional/negative exponents).

  • d/dx[x^(3/2)] = (3/2)x^(1/2).
  • d/dx[4/x²] = d/dx[4x^(−2)] = −8x^(−3) = −8/x³.

Example 3 (Product Rule). d/dx[x² sin x] = 2x·sin x + x²·cos x.

Example 4 (Quotient Rule). d/dx[(2x + 1)/(x − 1)] = (2(x−1) − (2x+1)(1))/(x−1)² = −3/(x−1)².

Example 5 (Higher-order). For f(x) = x⁵: f'(x) = 5x⁴, f''(x) = 20x³, f'''(x) = 60x².

Example 6 (Implicit). For x² + y² = 25: differentiate to get 2x + 2y·(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = −x/y. At (3, 4), the tangent slope is −3/4.

Example 7 (Inverse). For f(x) = x³ with inverse g, find g'(8). Since 2³ = 8, g(8) = 2. f'(x) = 3x², so f'(2) = 12. Thus g'(8) = 1/12.

quiz.q: The derivative of f(x) = (3x + 2)/(x - 1) is:
Given the function f(x) = 1/x, use the tangent line at x = 1 to approximate the value of f(1.1).
If f(x) = (x^2 + 3)^2, what is f'(x)?
Find the derivative of f(x) = sin(x) cos(x).
Find the derivative of f(x) = csc(x) + cot(x).
quiz.explanation: d/dx(csc x) = -csc x cot x and d/dx(cot x) = -csc^2 x.

topics.title: Graphical Interpretation, Common Mistakes & Tips
topics.concept:
Graphical Interpretation

  • f'(x) is the slope of the tangent to y = f(x) at x.
  • Where f is increasing, f' > 0; where decreasing, f' < 0; at a smooth peak/valley, f' = 0.
  • A corner ⇒ left and right tangent slopes differ ⇒ not differentiable.
  • A vertical tangent ⇒ f'(x) → ±∞ ⇒ not differentiable, even though the function may be continuous.
  • The graph of f' records the slopes of f; reading one from the other is a frequent exam skill (developed further in Unit 5).

Common Mistakes

  • Quotient Rule sign/order errors. It is (low·d-high − high·d-low)/low², not the reverse — the subtraction order matters.
  • Forgetting the Product Rule and writing d/dx[f·g] = f'·g' (wrong).
  • Dropping the dy/dx factor in implicit differentiation when differentiating a y-term.
  • Assuming continuity ⇒ differentiability. |x| is the classic counterexample at 0.
  • Power Rule on the wrong form. Rewrite roots and reciprocals as exponents first (√x = x^(1/2), 1/x² = x^(−2)).
  • Inverse-derivative confusion. g'(a) = 1/f'(g(a)), not 1/f'(a).

AP Exam Tips

  • Recognize limit definitions of the derivative in disguise — they are common multiple-choice items.
  • Know the six trig derivatives cold; the "co-" functions (cos, cot, csc) all carry a negative sign.
  • On implicit differentiation free-response, show the dy/dx factor explicitly — it earns method points.
  • For a tangent-line question: find the point and the slope f'(a), then use point-slope form.
  • Simplify only as needed; an unsimplified but correct derivative still earns full credit on free-response.

Unit Summary

  • The derivative is f'(x) = lim_{h→0} (f(x+h) − f(x))/h — a slope of a tangent and an instantaneous rate.
  • Differentiability ⇒ continuity, but not conversely (corners, cusps, vertical tangents break differentiability).
  • Master the Power, Product, Quotient rules and the six trig derivatives.
  • Implicit differentiation differentiates both sides in x (with dy/dx on y-terms); inverse derivatives use g'(a) = 1/f'(g(a)).
  • Higher-order derivatives are derivatives of derivatives.

Next unit: the Chain Rule and its combinations (composite, implicit, and inverse functions).

quiz.q: The derivative of f(x) = (x² - 3)(x³ + 2x + 1) is:
The derivative of f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x² + 3) is:

The position of a particle moving along a coordinate axis is given by s(t) = (1/3)t^3 - 2t^2 + 3t for t > 0. By the Mean Value Theorem, for what value of t in the open interval (0, 3) does the instantaneous velocity equal the average velocity of the particle on [0, 3]?
quiz.explanation: Average velocity on [0,3] = (s(3) - s(0))/3 = 0, since s(3) = 9 - 18 + 9 = 0 and s(0) = 0. Setting v(t) = t^2 - 4t + 3 = 0 gives t = 1 or t = 3; only t = 1 lies in the open interval (0, 3).

quiz.q: What is the value of the derivative of f(x) = csc(x) cot(x) at x = π/6?
quiz.explanation: Using the product rule: f'(x) = (-csc(x)cot(x))cot(x) + csc(x)(-csc^2(x)) = -csc(x)cot^2(x) - csc^3(x). At x = π/6, csc(π/6) = 2 and cot(π/6) = √3. Thus, f'(π/6) = -(2)(√3)^2 - (2)^3 = -2(3) - 8 = -6 - 8 = -14.

quiz.q: The derivative of f(x) = (x^2 + 1)(x^3 - 3x^2 + 2) is:

mock_tests.title: Practice Set A

questions.q: If f(x) = x sin(x), find f'(x).
questions.explanation: Using the product rule: f'(x) = (d/dx(x))sin(x) + x(d/dx(sin(x))) = (1)sin(x) + x(cos(x)) = sin(x) + x cos(x).

questions.q: What is the derivative of f(x) = tan(x)?
questions.explanation: The derivative of tan(x) is a standard trigonometric derivative formula: d/dx(tan(x)) = sec^2(x).

questions.q: Differentiate f(x) = x^2 cos(x).
questions.explanation: Using product rule: f'(x) = (d/dx(x^2))cos(x) + x^2(d/dx(cos(x))) = 2x cos(x) + x^2(-sin(x)) = 2x cos(x) - x^2 sin(x).

questions.q: If f(x) = 2x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x, what is the second derivative f''(x)?
Find dy/dx for the curve x^2 + y^2 = 25.
questions.explanation: Implicit differentiation: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Solving for dy/dx gives 2y(dy/dx) = -2x, so dy/dx = -x/y.

questions.q: A function f(x) is defined such that lim_{x→3} f(x) = f(3). Which of the following MUST be true?
options: The graph of f has a horizontal tangent at x = 3.
questions.explanation: The definition provided is the definition of continuity at a point: lim_{x→c} f(x) = f(c).

questions.q: What is the derivative of f(x) = sec(x)?
questions.explanation: The derivative of sec(x) is a standard trigonometric identity: d/dx(sec(x)) = sec(x)tan(x).

questions.q: Given f(1.9) = 2.7, f(2) = 3, and f(2.1) = 3.3, estimate f'(2) using the symmetric difference quotient.
The average rate of change of the function f(x) = x² + 3x - 5 over the interval [1, 4] is:
questions.explanation: The average rate of change is calculated as (f(4) - f(1)) / (4 - 1). f(4) = 16 + 12 - 5 = 23, f(1) = 1 + 3 - 5 = -1. Thus, (23 - (-1)) / 3 = 24 / 3 = 8.

questions.q: If the position of a particle is given by s(t) = t³ - 2t² + 4, the instantaneous velocity at t = 2 is:
Which of the following represents the derivative of f(x) = 1/x at x = 2 using the limit definition?
Given the table of values for f(x), estimate f'(2) if f(1.9) = 3.61, f(2) = 4, and f(2.1) = 4.41.
The slope of the tangent line to the curve y = sin(x) at x = π/2 is:
questions.explanation: The derivative of sin(x) is cos(x). At x = π/2, cos(π/2) = 0, so the slope is 0.

questions.q: Which of the following functions is NOT differentiable at x = 0?
questions.explanation: f(x) = |x| has a corner at x = 0, making it non-differentiable there. The other functions are smooth and differentiable everywhere.

questions.q: The derivative of f(x) = x⁴ - 3x² + 5x - 7 is:
questions.explanation: Applying the power rule: d/dx(x⁴) = 4x³, d/dx(-3x²) = -6x, d/dx(5x) = 5, d/dx(-7) = 0. Combined: 4x³ - 6x + 5.

questions.q: The derivative of f(x) = x⁻³ + 2x⁻¹ is:
questions.explanation: Applying the power rule: d/dx(x⁻³) = -3x⁻⁴, d/dx(2x⁻¹) = -2x⁻². Combined: -3x⁻⁴ - 2x⁻².

questions.q: The derivative of f(x) = 3sin(x) - 2cos(x) is:
questions.explanation: d/dx(3sin(x)) = 3cos(x), d/dx(-2cos(x)) = 2sin(x). Combined: 3cos(x) + 2sin(x).

questions.q: The derivative of f(x) = tan(x) is:
questions.explanation: The derivative of tan(x) is sec²(x).

questions.q: If f(x) = x⁴ - 2x³ + 5, then f''(x) is:
questions.explanation: First derivative: f'(x) = 4x³ - 6x². Second derivative: f''(x) = 12x² - 12x.

questions.q: A particle moves along the x-axis such that its position at time t is given by x(t) = 5t^2 - t^3. What is the instantaneous velocity of the particle at t = 2?

mock_tests.note: Auto-graded practice from the Differentiation: Definition and Fundamental Properties question bank.

mock_tests.title: Practice Set B

questions.q: The limit lim_{h→0} [cos(π/4 + h) - cos(π/4)] / h represents the derivative of which function at what value?
questions.explanation: The limit is the definition f'(a) = lim_{h→0} [f(a+h)-f(a)]/h. Here f(x)=cos(x) and a=π/4.

questions.q: Calculate d/dx [ (x+1)/(x-1) ].
If f(x) = sin(x), what is the 4th derivative f''''(x)?
questions.explanation: f' = cos, f'' = -sin, f''' = -cos, f'''' = sin.

questions.q: Estimate the derivative of f(x) at x = 2 using the data: f(1.9) = 10, f(2.1) = 12.
Which of the following is equivalent to d/dx [x^2 tan(x)]?
questions.explanation: Product rule: d/dx(x^2)tan(x) + x^2(d/dx tan(x)) = 2x tan(x) + x^2 sec^2(x). Both B and C represent this sum.

questions.q: The instantaneous rate of change of y = e^x at x = ln(2) is:
questions.explanation: The derivative of e^x is e^x. At x = ln(2), e^{ln(2)} = 2.

questions.q: Using the limit definition, the derivative of f(x) = 2x + 1 at x = 3 is:
The derivative of f(x) = √x at x = 9 using the limit definition is:

questions.explanation: Symmetric difference quotient: f'(2) ~ (5.61 - 4.41)/0.2 = 1.2/0.2 = 6.

questions.q: The slope of the tangent line to y = cos(x) at x = π is:
questions.explanation: The derivative of cos(x) is -sin(x). At x = π, -sin(π) = 0.

questions.q: The derivative of f(x) = x^(-1/2) is:
questions.explanation: Applying the power rule: d/dx(x^(-1/2)) = (-1/2)x^(-3/2).

questions.q: The derivative of f(x) = cot(x) is:
questions.explanation: The derivative of cot(x) is -csc²(x).

questions.q: The derivative of f(x) = (x + 1)(x² - 2x) is:
The average rate of change of a function f on the interval [a, b] is represented by which of the following?
options: f'(c) for some c in (a, b)
questions.explanation: The average rate of change is the slope of the secant line passing through (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)), which is [f(b) - f(a)] / (b - a).

questions.q: If f(x) = x^2, what is the value of lim_{h→0} [(x+h)^2 - x^2] / h?
questions.explanation: This is the definition of the derivative of f(x) = x^2. By the power rule, f'(x) = 2x.

questions.q: A function f is differentiable at x = 3 with f(3) = 2 and f'(3) = -4. What is the equation of the line tangent to f at x = 3?
questions.explanation: The point-slope form of a line is y - y1 = m(x - x1). Here, (x1, y1) = (3, 2) and m = -4.

questions.q: For which of the following values of x does the graph of f(x) = |x - 5| have a derivative that does not exist?
questions.explanation: The function f(x) = |x - 5| has a sharp corner (v-shape) at x = 5, where the slope changes abruptly from -1 to 1.

questions.q: Find f'(x) for f(x) = 5x^4 - 2x^2 + 7.
questions.explanation: Apply the power rule: d/dx(5x^4) = 20x^3, d/dx(-2x^2) = -4x, and d/dx(7) = 0.

questions.q: If f(x) = 3 sin(x) + 2 cos(x), find f'(x).
questions.explanation: The derivative of sin(x) is cos(x) and the derivative of cos(x) is -sin(x). Thus, f'(x) = 3 cos(x) + 2(-sin(x)) = 3 cos(x) - 2 sin(x).

questions.q: What is the derivative of f(x) = tan(x) + sec(x)?
questions.explanation: d/dx(tan x) = sec^2(x) and d/dx(sec x) = sec(x)tan(x).
